Folic acid protects against the development of neural tube defects (p.1942) and supplementation during pregnancy is advised; vitamin B12 supplementation may also be warranted. Vitamin A, however, may be teratogenic and maximum intakes in pregnancy have been recommended, see p.1972. The risks to the fetus of untreated maternal hypopar- athyroidism are considered greater than the risks of hypercal- caemia due to vitamin D therapy (see p.1988). Systematic reviews1,2 of supplementation in pregnancy lacked enough data to indicate whether vitamin C or E, alone or with other supplements, were of benefit. There was some suggestion of decreased risk of developing pre-eclampsia with either vita- min C or E; however, preterm births may have increased with vitamin C supplementation. 1. Rumbold A, Crowther CA. Vitamin C supplementation in preg- nancy. Available in The Cochrane Database of Systematic Re- views; Issue 1. Chichester: John Wiley; 2005 (accessed 13/01/06). 2.
